↳ Posted by dafydd on February 28th, 2003.

↳ Posted by Kenny on November 17th, 2003.

4th part

Here is the 4th part as I have it:

M: 6/8
K: Bmin
|:aga f2e|fBB f2e|aga f2e|cAA fec|
aga f2e|fBB f2 e|fga efa|cAA fec:|

It’s just a slight variation on the 2nd part.

I’ve heard the tune played slightly differently, with the 7th bar of every part as: |fga efa| instead of |fga e2a|.

Being part of the Highland Bagpipe repertoire, it must have two sharps in th key signature (BTW it is B minor, not D major), but string players sometimes sharpen the Gs (making it B dorian).

Paddy’s Leather Breeches

There’s a hint there in what ceolachan has posted, but nobody seems to have said it outright: this transcription has the wrong key signature. It should be in B dorian ie with 3 sharps.

↳ Posted by ethical blend on April 13th, 2008.

2 sharps

There are no G sharps in Highland bagpipe music. And there are mistakes in the 3rd part of the sheet music - this transcription is best avoided. It’s in 42 tune-books - that’s 42 players playing a sheight version of a classic pipe jig. This should be deleted.

↳ Posted by Kenny on April 13th, 2008.

Paddy’s Leather Breeches, X:6

This is based on version 4 above but with the final bar of each line modified and line 6 changed; as played by many pipe bands.
